                                   1   G.       Exhibit List

                                  12   L.     Jury Instructions
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13          The parties shall file a joint set of proposed jury instructions by the Deadline to File

                                  14   Pretrial Documents. These shall also be emailed to tshpo@cand.uscourts.gov in Microsoft Word

                                  15   format. Jury instructions should conform to the Manual of Model Civil Jury Instructions for the

                                  17   contents. Any instruction on which the parties cannot agree shall be marked as “disputed” and

                                  18   included in the joint instructions where the party proposing the instruction believes it should be

                                  19   given. Argument for and against each disputed instruction shall be included on a separate page

                                  20   directly following the disputed instruction. The Court shall hear oral argument on the disputed

                                  21   jury instructions at the close of Defendant’s case in chief.

                                  22   M.     Proposed Verdict Forms
                                  23          The parties shall file a joint proposed verdict form by the Deadline to File Pretrial

                                  24   Documents. If unable to stipulate to a verdict form, each side shall submit a proposed verdict

                                  28   Floor, 450 Golden Gate Avenue, San Francisco, California. Lead counsel who will try the case

                                  13             Plaintiff Meta Platforms, Inc. (“Meta”) brings this action against Defendants Judang Team
                                  14   LLC (“Judang”), Perfeos LLC (“Perfeos”), Jot & Journeys (“J&J”), and Antonio Jose Liévano
                                  15   (collectively, “Defendants”), alleging that Defendants operated a deceptive and misleading
                                  16   advertising scheme on Meta’s social media platforms and improperly obtained advertising credit
                                  17   lines from Meta. ECF No. 1. On January 20, 2026, the Court granted Counsel’s1 motion to
                                  18   withdraw as counsel for all Defendants on the condition that Counsel remain counsel of record to
                                  19   serve all filed documents on Defendants until a substitution of counsel is filed. ECF No. 57. For
                                  20   all such documents, the Court ordered Counsel to e-file proof of service within three business days
                                  21   of filing. Id.
                                  22             On February 5, 2026, Defendants Perfeos, J&J, and Liévano filed an answer to the

                                  24   Judang.

                                  27

                                            Case 3:25-cv-05156-TSH           Document 74        Filed 03/03/26      Page 2 of 3




                                   1   February 10, 2026. The Court then issued an order on February 13, 2026, reminding Counsel of

                                   2   their service obligation and directing Counsel to serve Judang with the answer by February 19,

                                   3   2026. ECF No. 60. On February 19, 2026, Counsel filed an affidavit indicating they had effected

                                   4   service on Perfeos.2 ECF No. 61.

                                   5             On February 20, 2026, the Court ordered that default be entered against Judang. ECF No.

                                   6   64. In this order, the Court reminded Counsel of their service obligation and ordered Counsel to

                                   7   serve Judang with the default order no later than February 25, 2026. Id. Also on February 20,

                                   9   See ECF Nos. 63, 65. Counsel has not filed an attestation that they served Judang with the

                                  11   orders.

                                  12             Since February 20, 2026, several more filings have occurred on the docket, including the
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   Clerk’s Notice of Entry of Default against Judang. See ECF Nos. 68, 70, 71, 72. The Court

                                  14   should not have to hunt Counsel down every time a filing occurs to ensure that Counsel comply

                                  16             “Civil contempt . . . consists of a party’s disobedience to a specific and definite court order

                                  17   by failure to take all reasonable steps within the party’s power to comply.” Inst. of Cetacean

                                  18   Rsch. v. Sea Shepherd Conservation Soc’y, 774 F.3d 935, 945 (9th Cir. 2014) (citation omitted).

                                  19   “When there has been contempt, a court can levy contempt sanctions pursuant to its inherent

                                  20   powers.” Dionisio v. Midland Credit Mgmt., No. 1:19-cv-0190-DAD-JLT, 2019 WL 2420403, at

                                  21   *2 (E.D. Cal. June 10, 2019) (citing Cooke v. United States, 267 U.S. 517, 539 (1925)). A

                                  22   “district court has wide latitude in determining whether there has been contemptuous defiance of

                                  23   its order.” Hook v. Arizona Dep’t of Corr., 107 F.3d 1397, 1403 (9th Cir. 1997) (cleaned up).

                                  24             “A court may wield its civil contempt powers for two separate and independent purposes:

                                  25   (1) to coerce the defendant into compliance with the court’s order; and (2) to compensate the

                                  26   complainant for losses sustained.” Shell Offshore Inc. v. Greenpeace, Inc., 815 F.3d 623, 629 (9th

                                       stating that service was effected on Judang. ECF No. 62.

                                   1   Cir. 2016) (cleaned up). “Because civil compensatory sanctions are remedial, they typically take

                                   2   the form of unconditional monetary sanctions; whereas coercive civil sanctions, intended to deter,

                                   3   generally take the form of conditional fines.” Id. For example, courts may impose monetary

                                   4   sanctions for every day of non-compliance to coerce parties or attorneys into compliance with

                                   5   court orders. See Dionisio, 2019 WL 2420403, at *3 (ordering monetary sanctions of $100 per

                                   6   day for every business day parties fail to comply with the court’s orders); W. States Insulators &

                                   7   Allied Workers Pension Plan v. Jenco Mech. Insulation, Inc., No. C-11-0175-EMC, 2013 WL

                                   8   2252004, at *4 (N.D. Cal. May 22, 2013) (ordering coercive monetary sanctions of $100 per day

                                   9   for every day of non-compliance with court’s orders “given Defendant’s evasive behavior and

                                  10   non-responsiveness”).

                                  11            Twice the Court has ordered Counsel to comply with the Court’s order at ECF No. 57

                                  12   regarding service on Judang. See ECF Nos. 60, 64. Despite these reminders—and the Court’s
Northern District of California
 United States District Court




                                  13   initial order granting Counsel’s withdrawal—Counsel continue to ignore the Court’s orders by not

                                  14   timely effecting service on Judang.

                                  15            Accordingly, the Court hereby ORDERS Counsel (James C. Huber, Bradley C. Crosley,

                                  16   and Darren Cruz) to show cause why they should not be held in contempt of the Court’s orders

                                  17   and sanctioned for failure to comply with the Court’s orders imposing service obligations on

                                  18   Counsel. Counsel shall file a written response no later than March 10, 2026.

                                  19            Notice is hereby provided that failure to file a written response may result in the Court

                                  20   imposing sanctions. Thus, it is imperative the Court receive a written response by the deadline

                                  21   above.

                                  22            IT IS SO ORDERED.
